publicPresentation.hanjaUsage: Secondary traditional detail behind progressive disclosure

pairSemantics.directionalRequirement: A directional claim must cite directional evidence and declare reverse-participants swap semantics.

publicFigure.allowedFraming: A hypothetical pair reading for the user's reflection, based on a sourced public birth record.

temporalPolicy.approximate: A claim is definitive only when it is common across every retained chart variant; otherwise show correlated alternatives and a limitation.
temporalPolicy.disputed: A claim is definitive only when it is common across every retained chart variant; otherwise show correlated alternatives and a limitation.

allowedEvidenceClasses.purpose: A deterministic compatibility result from a versioned rule accepted under Issue #33 review.
Availability and limitation handling only; it cannot create a compatibility claim.
Marks a reviewed rule output as invariant across every retained approximate or disputed variant.
Carries non-definitive reviewed rule alternatives without averaging or selecting one chart.

candidateTraditionalSignalFamilies.requirement: No dimension claim is allowed until a versioned deterministic Issue #33 rule maps the evidence and passes review.
Not emitted by the current derived-feature package and never implicitly required by this taxonomy. Any future adoption needs explicit methodology review.

dimensions.description: How a pair may naturally pace back-and-forth conversation.

poles.label: Reflective
poles.description: More space to think before responding.

dimensions.allowedExample: You may enjoy quick exchanges, while leaving a little thinking room can help both of you feel heard.
limits: Does not measure intelligence, honesty, interest, or communication skill.

dimensions.description: How quickly a pair may prefer to move from options to a choice.

poles.label: Spontaneous
poles.description: More comfort choosing in the moment.

dimensions.allowedExample: One useful check-in is whether this choice needs more time or feels ready now.
limits: Does not measure competence, maturity, or responsibility.

dimensions.description: How a pair may balance plans with room to adjust.

poles.label: Structured
poles.description: More ease with plans and clear expectations.

poles.label: Adaptive
poles.description: More ease changing course as things unfold.

dimensions.allowedExample: A light plan with an agreed place to improvise may suit both rhythms.
limits: Does not predict reliability or chaos.
Both structure and adaptation can be caring responses.

dimensions.description: How a pair may balance individual space with shared time.

poles.label: Independent space
poles.description: More energy from protected individual time.

poles.label: Shared time
poles.description: More energy from doing things together.

dimensions.allowedExample: Naming what counts as quality time—and what counts as restorative solo time—may reduce guesswork.
limits: Does not diagnose attachment style or commitment.
Does not assume monogamy, cohabitation, or any relationship structure.

dimensions.description: How a pair may prefer to pause, revisit, or reconnect after tension.

poles.label: Pause first
poles.description: More room to settle before revisiting tension.

dimensions.allowedExample: Agreeing on when to revisit a tense moment can make different repair rhythms easier to navigate.
limits: Does not predict abuse, violence, safety, blame, or moral character.
A compatibility result never replaces a real safety assessment.

dimensions.description: How a pair may approach coordinating a shared goal.

poles.label: Divide and own
poles.description: More ease taking separate ownership of parts.

poles.label: Build together
poles.description: More ease working side by side.

dimensions.allowedExample: You might clarify which parts feel better owned separately and which feel better built together.
limits: Does not measure ambition, leadership, or worth.
It makes no claim about money or financial habits.

dimensions.description: How a pair may balance familiar experiences with trying something new.

poles.label: Familiar
poles.description: More comfort deepening known routines and places.

poles.label: Exploratory
poles.description: More energy from new settings and experiences.

dimensions.allowedExample: Alternating a favorite ritual with a new plan can give both preferences room.
limits: Does not measure courage, sophistication, or growth potential.
Familiarity and novelty are both context-dependent.

dimensions.description: How a pair may differ in when and how readily feelings are put into words.

poles.label: Private processing
poles.description: More time to understand a feeling before sharing it.

poles.label: Outward expression
poles.description: More ease naming a feeling as it happens.

dimensions.allowedExample: A gentle check-in can leave room for both immediate expression and later reflection.
limits: Does not diagnose mental health, empathy, emotional availability, or love.
Expression style is not emotional depth.

excludedV1Dimensions.reason: Insufficient reviewed support; wealthworthiness and financial predictions are prohibited.
